hypothesis: After the code is written and rspec/eslint pass, every run spends 8-15 more calls on a live-UI check: app start, hand-seeding a user, fighting the onboarding modal, Playwright login and page choice. These calls carry 45-56k of context each, so they cost roughly 400-600k tokens, about half of a run. In the runs I read, this tail never found a real feature bug. Replacing it with a static registration and string check, in one batched grep call, removes those calls and keeps eslint and rspec as the feedback loop.
changeSummary: Only system-prompt.md changes: the Verification section no longer asks for app start, Playwright, user seeding or a live UI check. It now asks for eslint on all touched JS plus a node parse of the locale JSON, one batched grep confirming everything is registered and the spec's exact accessible names and strings are present, rspec specs that cover the spec's API behaviours, and a git status cleanup. The tools=["Bash"] config and the rest of the prompt are unchanged.

 Verification (do each at most once unless it fails; filter output to failures only, e.g. grep for examples/failures/errors):
 - Run migrations for development and test (RAILS_ENV=test), then rspec only on your new specs plus the closely related existing spec directories (api controllers, models, services). Do not run the entire suite.
-- Run eslint on the touched javascript. Do not run npm run build or a separate webpack build: `/opt/frugal/task/app start` already compiles the assets (several minutes, run it once, give it a long timeout, never poll with sleep, and avoid restarting it).
-- After the app is up, use ONE combined Playwright script via /opt/frugal/task/pw-node that checks the API with a token and the UI (the new toggle in the status action bar, the new list column showing the saved status). Seed the user and token with a single rails runner call. A fresh user sees an onboarding introduction modal in the web UI unless the user's web settings record has a high introductionVersion, and the account must be confirmed/approved; set these when seeding. Print only short results. Allow at most two attempts at debugging the harness itself; if the UI check keeps failing for harness reasons, stop fiddling with screenshots and finish, since the code review of the diff plus the API check is enough. Fix real feature bugs, not harness quirks.
-- Then run `app stop`, check `git status` for stray files you created in the repo (remove scratch files), and finish.
+- Run eslint on every touched or new javascript file (it also catches unresolved imports and syntax errors), and parse the touched locale json files with node.
+- Do NOT start the app, use Playwright, seed users or tokens, or run webpack or npm run build. In earlier runs the live-UI check cost 8-12 extra calls (onboarding modal, login, page choice) and never found a real bug; the evaluator boots the app and checks UI and API itself. Instead make the frontend correct by construction: mirror the closest existing analogue one-to-one, and in ONE batched grep call confirm that every new action, reducer, route, column, navigation entry and component is registered and imported where its analogue is, and that the exact accessible names and locale strings from the spec appear in the component and in en.json.
+- Your own rspec specs must cover the API behaviours in the spec (errors, pagination links, ownership, the boost case). Fix any real failure once, then stop.
+- Check `git status` for stray files you created in the repo (remove scratch files), and finish.
 
 Finish with a summary of at most three sentences.
evidence: Run 2304e9 (792k, 20 calls): calls 1-10 build and run rspec, reaching 44.4k context. Calls 11-19 are harness work: seed script, Playwright edits, grep for introductionVersion and Web::Setting, rails runner to set the setting, swapping the page. That is 9 calls at 44-49k, about 420k of the 793k. Run 0e8a32 (1.08M, 25 calls): the calls after the app starts are seeding, repeated "Welcome to the fediverse" modal failures, and 3-4 attempts at the introductionVersion value (9999, 99999999, 99999999999999). The final calls cost 50-56k each and no feature bug was fixed there. The only real fix, a 404 expectation in a spec, came from rspec before the app started. Run ca4f9b (exp-0006, uiseed helper, 1.08M, 25 calls): it still ran calls 11-25 at 46-56k each, so a helper that eases the UI harness did not remove the tail. The tail itself is what has to go. Cache read is 92% of tokens, so removing whole calls is the lever.
expectedSavings: Runs currently take 19-25 calls. Without the tail they should take about 10-12, finishing at about 45k context. Per-call cost drops from about 45-55k to about 30-45k on the calls that remain. Estimate: remove 9-13 calls × about 48k ≈ 430-620k, so the median should fall from about 880k to about 400-500k. Main risk: a UI-check failure in the hidden evaluator that the live check would have caught, for example a wrong reducer key or a missing registration. The grep-based registration check, eslint's unresolved-import detection and the instruction to mirror the favourites analogue one-to-one mitigate this. If one of the 5 verification runs fails a UI check, the candidate is rejected. A smaller secondary risk is that the agent ignores the prohibition and starts the app anyway, which would only revert to the current cost.
